model_card.name: postsynaptic L1-normalized LIF (Banana Quest l1_lif)

free_parameters.target_input_mv: postsynaptic 总输入预算（mV）；以 sim-core ti=3.0×7mV=21mV 为锚点粗扫，取核心层全种子通过的最宽窗口，不按任务逐拟合

model_card.normalization: postsynaptic L1: w_ij ← w_ij / Σ_i|w_ij| × target_input_mv（保留符号），与 Banana Quest game/src/sim-core.js 一致
model_card.sign_rule: snedea/flybrain NT_SIGN（GLUT 兴奋性；histamine 无类别）
model_card.fit_data: target_input_mv 经粗扫（不针对任何单任务拟合）
model_card.conflict_of_interest: 无；本项目为第三方提交，非 flybench 官方认证

tasks.title: Silence in, silence out

checks.description: network rate[baseline] < 0.5 Hz  [3/3 seeds, sd 0]
checks.basis: Shiu et al. 2024 (silent without input); convention: 0.5 Hz mean over all neurons is below any spontaneous rate reported in fly recordings

checks.description: active fraction[baseline] < 0.01  [3/3 seeds, sd 0]
checks.basis: convention: fewer than 1% of neurons may fire spontaneously in 1 s; the fly brain at rest is not silent (Shiu 2024 Fig. 1), but its spontaneous activity is not reproduced by this model class

tasks.title: Sugar → proboscis extension

checks.description: rate[sugar] > 5.0 Hz  [0/3 seeds, sd 0]
checks.basis: convention: 5 Hz over the window is ~2.5 spikes per neuron, the smallest response that is unambiguously not noise (baseline is 0 Hz)

checks.description: rate[sugar] / rate[baseline] > 5.0  [0/3 seeds, sd 0]  [floored: every compared condition silent]
checks.basis: convention: a 5x rise over baseline; baseline is ~0 Hz so any real response clears this easily — it exists to fail models whose baseline is already high

checks.description: active fraction[sugar] < 0.1  [3/3 seeds, sd 5.86e-06]
checks.basis: convention: Shiu et al. 2024 report sparse activity on stimulation; 10% of all neurons is a generous ceiling chosen so a healthy sparse response passes and mass recruitment fails

tasks.title: Bitter suppresses the sugar response

checks.description: rate[sugar] > 5.0 Hz  [0/3 seeds, sd 0]
checks.basis: convention: 5 Hz over the window is ~2.5 spikes per neuron, the smallest response that is unambiguously not noise (baseline is 0 Hz)

checks.description: rate[sugar_plus_bitter] / rate[sugar] < 0.5  [0/3 seeds, sd 0]  [floored: every compared condition silent]
checks.basis: Shiu et al. 2024 Fig. 3 (bitter co-activation abolishes MN9 response in the model); Jaeger et al. 2018 (bitter suppresses PER behaviourally). 0.5 is a convention: half is the smallest suppression worth calling suppression

tasks.title: Looming → giant fiber escape

checks.description: rate[loom] > 5.0 Hz  [0/3 seeds, sd 0]
checks.basis: convention: 5 Hz over the 280 ms window is >1 GF spike per neuron. NOTE the real GF fires a single spike per escape (von Reyn et al. 2014); this check tests that the pathway conducts, task 13 tests the spike count

checks.description: rate[loom] / rate[baseline] > 5.0  [0/3 seeds, sd 0]  [floored: every compared condition silent]
checks.basis: convention: a 5x rise over baseline; baseline is ~0 Hz so any real response clears this easily — it exists to fail models whose baseline is already high

checks.description: active fraction[loom] < 0.1  [3/3 seeds, sd 3.39e-06]
checks.basis: convention: Shiu et al. 2024 report sparse activity on stimulation; 10% of all neurons is a generous ceiling chosen so a healthy sparse response passes and mass recruitment fails

tasks.title: Bitter alone does not extend the proboscis

checks.description: rate[bitter] < 2.0 Hz  [3/3 seeds, sd 0]
checks.basis: Shiu et al. 2024 (bitter alone does not drive MN9); convention: 2 Hz is <1 spike per neuron per window, i.e. effectively silent

checks.description: active fraction[bitter] < 0.1  [3/3 seeds, sd 0]
checks.basis: convention: Shiu et al. 2024 report sparse activity on stimulation; 10% of all neurons is a generous ceiling chosen so a healthy sparse response passes and mass recruitment fails

tasks.title: Proboscis response scales with sugar intensity

checks.description: rate[measured] > 5.0 Hz  [0/3 seeds, sd 0]
checks.basis: Zhang, Guo & Montell 2016 (Neuron 91:863): labellar sugar GRN fires ~40 spikes/500 ms (≈80 Hz) at 100 mM sucrose, a concentration that reliably evokes PER; the pathway must conduct at the recorded input rate, not only at the 100 Hz convention

checks.description: rate[weak] > 1.0 Hz  [0/3 seeds, sd 0]
checks.basis: Dethier 1976; Dahanukar et al. 2007 (PER probability rises with sucrose concentration); convention: 1 Hz = a detectable weak response

checks.description: rate[strong] > 5.0 Hz  [0/3 seeds, sd 0]
checks.basis: convention: 5 Hz over the window is ~2.5 spikes per neuron, the smallest response that is unambiguously not noise (baseline is 0 Hz)

checks.description: rate[weak] / rate[strong] < 0.6  [0/3 seeds, sd 0]  [floored: every compared condition silent]
checks.basis: convention: a 5x weaker stimulus should give a visibly weaker response; 0.6 is lenient on purpose

checks.description: rate[strong] < 300.0 Hz  [3/3 seeds, sd 0]
checks.basis: convention: 300 Hz is above any sustained motor-neuron rate reported in insects; no MN9 electrophysiology exists (Schwarz et al. 2017 is optogenetic/kinematic), so this is a ceiling by convention; above it the readout is saturating, not responding

tasks.title: Repeated sugar gives a smaller second response

checks.description: rate[co2, ln23] > 5.0 Hz  [3/3 seeds, sd 0.85]
checks.basis: bioRxiv 2026.01.05.697655: LN23 relays CO2 through an extraglomerular pathway and is necessary for CO2 avoidance (1,771 ORN_V synapses onto the four LN23 in FlyWire); 5 Hz task-02 convention

checks.description: rate[co2, pnm1] > 5.0 Hz  [0/3 seeds, sd 0]

checks.description: rate[ovien_plus_oviin, ovidn] / rate[ovien] < 0.5  [0/3 seeds, sd 0.246]

checks.description: rate[pc1, oviin] > 5.0 Hz  [0/3 seeds, sd 0]
